```
<<<explanation: Ownership in Rust>>>
Every value in Rust has a single **owner**. When the owner goes out of scope,
the value is dropped.

```rust
let s = String::from("hi"); // s owns the String
```

Assigning a heap value to another variable *moves* it.

<<<code_snippet 1: Moving a String>>>
// code snippet: Shows how ownership moves between variables
```rust
fn main() {
    let s1 = String::from("hello");
    let s2 = s1; // s1 is moved into s2
    println!("{}", s2);
}
```

<<<code_snippet 2: Borrowing: references>>>
// code snippet: Borrow instead of moving
```rust
fn len(s: &String) -> usize {
    s.len()
}
```

<<<exercise 1: Fix the move>>>
// exercise description: Make this program compile without cloning
```rust
fn main() {
    let s = String::from("hi");
    let t = s;
    println!("{} {}", s, t);
}
```
